margin.claim_rule: H1 is carried by the LEAST favourable seed. The direction must hold in every seed; the pooled mean may be reported alongside but cannot carry the claim.
margin.measured_against: each seed's OWN session-1 (depth-1) score, never a pooled mean across seeds
margin.reporting: the per-seed vectors first, then min/median/max of each per-seed margin
margin.why_not_pooled: Pooling lets a favourable initialisation pay for an unfavourable one: the drop H1 asserts would then be a property of the pool, and no single run in the pool would exhibit it. The statement is about an arm dropping below its own baseline, so the baseline has to belong to the run that drops.

armB_seed_protocol.margin_rule_as_ruled: the registered margin is not adjusted to fit the observed spread; spreading past the margin costs the claim its decidability, not the margin its value

arm_A_noise_floor_not_transferable.why: That floor is arm A's, measured on arm A's rows and registered against arm A's cells. It is recorded here only to say it must not be borrowed for arm B.

measured_basis.reading: The two runs differed only in how the model was initialised, and the invention rate -- the class that fails the exit code -- moved by more than the registered margin by itself. A margin cannot be quoted against a background that large without saying what the background is.

armB_seed_protocol.plain_statement: A single seed cannot support H1. H1 is a claim about a DROP relative to a baseline the same run establishes -- session-1 of that very seed -- so one seed supplies one baseline and one later score and no distribution at all. There is nothing in a single seed that can distinguish 'this arm forgets' from 'this initialisation happened to sit there'.

r13_scope.applies_to: arm A rows only. The registered tolerance cells are arm-A cells (learn/1/reasked, learn/1/restarted).
r13_scope.arm_B_within_depth: arm B's live, reasked and restarted phases are identical within a depth (measured in the pair artifact: phase-identical = True), because arm B has no time-gated path -- its only forgetting is across depths. There is therefore no within-depth forgetting for R13 to tolerate in arm B, and no R13 cell to widen.

seeds.each_seed_is: a complete three-depth run (depths 1, 2, 3) of the same manifest and config, merged into its own artifact -- not one depth per seed

armB_seed_protocol.status: RULED by the PI as D-MPE8-06. Three seeds, each a complete three-depth run; the margin is measured against each seed's own session-1 score; H1 is carried by the least favourable seed. A single-seed run cannot support H1.
armB_seed_protocol.undecidable_rule: If the observed seed spread at a tier exceeds the registered margin (5.0 pp, unchanged), H1 is reported NOT DECIDABLE at that tier rather than passed. The instrument's instability is then the finding. Same discipline as H3/C4: an unmeasurable claim is named, not renumbered.
armB_seed_protocol.what_this_does_not_change: No sealed number is re-measured or moved. H1's registered margin of 5.0 pp is untouched and is put to the PI in D-MPE8-06 rather than silently revised, because the measured across-initialisation spread is what calls it into question.

within_seed_determinism.consequence: Re-running one seed at a fixed thread count returns the identical artifact. It can catch a broken tool and nothing else, so repeats of a fixed seed are NOT the noise measurement -- the variance H1 has to survive is across seeds.
within_seed_determinism.thread_count_is_part_of_the_configuratio: torch.set_num_threads(6) is pinned in the tool for this reason: the same seed at a different thread count moves the confidence in the eighth decimal, and the abstention threshold sits in a dense confidence region.

premise_checked_and_corrected.as_measured: arm B tier-40 session-1 = 12/136 = 8.82%; tier-120 session-1 = 6.25-7.4519%. Ratio 1.18x, not ~4x. The 20s figure belongs to arm A at tier 40 (38/136 = 27.94%).

Registering the wrong baseline would have made the floor reading look like a forgetting reading.

armB_tier120_interpretation.the_different_finding_it_points_at: 'it forgot' and 'it never knew' produce the same small absolute drop and are different results. At 6.25-7.4519% session-1 accuracy there is little stored to lose, and arm B has never been measured above 8.82% at session 1 at any tier. The artifacts already carry the evidence for the floor reading: per-depth retention shows items counted lost at depth 2 and 3 that were not held at session 1 (see retention_per_seed_per_depth in the verdict artifact). This block records that the tier-120 drop statistic cannot distinguish the two readings; it does not decide between them.
armB_tier120_interpretation.the_property_being_stated: arm B's session-1 live correct rate is 8.82% at tier 40 and 6.25-7.4519% at tier 120: low at both, and the tier-40 figure is only 1.18x the best tier-120 one. The registered margin is 5.0 percentage points, chosen against a 0.30% clone noise floor. Against a baseline of 6.25%, a 5.0 pp drop is 80.0% of everything the least favourable seed ever got right at session 1 -- and against arm B's own tier-40 baseline it is 56.7% of it. The margin is a percentage-point figure applied to a percentage-point-scale phenomenon sitting near the floor of the battery, at every tier measured. That is a property of the comparison, not of any one run.

cross_tier_comparability_regime_break.statement: Constraint (b) requires every content word a probe ask uses to be in that tier's taught set. Tiers 120 and 300 are built to satisfy it and the checker refuses an emit that does not. Tier 40 does NOT satisfy it: 8 of its 136 sealed probe asks use a content word that appears in no taught sentence -- 'what rings in the tower', 'how many dogs sleep', 'when does the bell toll', 'what does Mira love most'. So the baseline tier and the scaled tiers are not the same instrument: they differ in a DEFINITIONAL way that has nothing to do with memory, and any cross-tier difference in refusal rate is partly that difference and not forgetting.

Deleting the 8 asks changes the matrix; teaching 'tower' and 'many' changes tier 40's item set. Both would move the baseline to meet the new rule, which is the R2 failure mode wearing a cleanup as a costume.

A non-empty list means at least one file this seal hashes is not yet in the commit it names -- the seal is anchored to a commit that cannot reproduce it. Stamping a second registration right after the first is NOT that case, because registrations are excluded from every seal.
procedure: 2. run registration_seal.py <registration.json>   # git_head now contains those blobs
4. registration_seal.py <registration.json> --check   # must be clean at that HEAD
stamp_ordering.rule: COMMIT FIRST, THEN STAMP, THEN COMMIT THE STAMP. Never stamp while a file this seal hashes is uncommitted -- that is what git_dirty_sealed reports, not mere tree dirt.
stamp_ordering.why: git_head is the commit the seal claims to describe. If the sealed bytes are still uncommitted when the stamp is taken, git_head names a commit that does not contain them, and there is no checkout you can verify the seal against.

D-MPE8-03.consequence_for_the_plan: The plan's three tiers assume a pool 3x and 7.5x larger than the one arm A ships with. Tier 40 is authorable and sealed; tiers 120 and 300 need new material, which is a specification input the plan has not supplied. G2's go criteria require complete sealed artifacts AT ALL THREE TIERS, so on the current pool G2 cannot be met by any amount of running. measured.breakdown: 24 tell frames (all distinct) + 16 QA answers (all distinct by the stated heuristic) = 40, exactly one pair per item, no pair reused
measured.why_the_cross_product_does_not_count: Multiplying subjects by verbs is not the same pool. 'the rain bites the latch' is a new sentence with new semantics; generating 851 grammatical fakes from a 40-item pool is inventing items, which is what the ruling forbids. The number that answers the ruling's question is the union of pairs the pool actually contains.

D-MPE8-03.reasoning: Extending the curriculum is data work. Inventing items to fill a tier changes what forgetting means, and that is a specification edit.

constraints.a: new items use the SAME registered frame grammar (who/what <verb>s the <object>, and QA pairs of the same shape classes) so the shape arbiter and probe construction apply unchanged
constraints.b: every content word a new item introduces is itself in the taught set for that tier, so the word-level grader's trace set stays well-defined and C2 keeps its meaning
constraints.c: the probe matrix scales proportionally from the registered 136 at tier 40 and each tier keeps its guarded-absence and distractor rows, defined as not in that tier's taught set
constraints.d: register the construction rule, the seed, the item counts and the distinct-subject-verb-pair count BEFORE any run, and commit the emitted tier files with their curriculum_sha256

ruling_second.decision: Authoring tiers 120 and 300 REQUIRES extending the item pool, and that is permitted -- the plan demands 120 and 300 taught items, which the current 40 cannot be. The forbidden thing is changing what forgetting means, so bind the extension to constraints (a)-(d) that keep the definition fixed. Stop again only if the vocabulary cannot be extended without inventing words no arm could ever be taught.
ruling_second.finding_constraint_c_is_false_as_written: The ruling says guarded-absence rows 'scale naturally'. Measured: the registered 24 guarded-absence rows come from TWO item ids (tell1.2 'the bell hangs on the wall' and pair1.0 'where does the bell hang?' -- the same fact, taught twice), in the teach arm only, at depths 2 and 3, across live/reasked/restarted: 2 x 2 x 3 x 1 arm = 24 (measured from armA_tier40_newenv.json, not inferred). It is not a per-item quantity, so it does not scale with tier size by any mechanism I can point at. The distractor rows DO scale (12 -> 36 -> 90 by construction). Reported rather than quietly reinterpreted: at tiers 120/300 the guarded-absence count is an outcome to be measured, not a number the construction guarantees.

authored.authored_under: D-MPE8-03 as ruled 2026-11-03: extending the item pool is permitted; changing what forgetting means is not, so the extension is bound to constraints (a)-(d) and each is checked at emit time by tools/mp_e8_curriculum.py check_tier().

confound_registered.name: tier-size confound on refusal, NOT on the forgetting curve
confound_registered.reporting_rule: Refusal-rate change across tiers is reported SEPARATELY from the forgetting curve. A tier-120 or tier-300 result must not be read as forgetting unless the refusal-rate movement is accounted for on its own line. This is a pre-registered confound, not a post-hoc excuse: it is written before any tier 120/300 artifact exists.
confound_registered.statement: The coverage floor and the arbiter were tuned at 40 items. At 120 and 300 items the same floor may move refusal rates for reasons that have nothing to do with memory: more distractor rows, more vocabulary to cover, a larger taught set for the word-level grader to trace.

constraints_checked.a_frame_grammar: every new tell is an svo call whose surface == stem + 's' and whose ask word is what/who; a lemma that does not take a plain +s third person is rejected before anything is drawn (this fired: brush, catch, sketch, stitch, touch, mix, polish, dry were removed from the lexicon because the rule would have emitted 'brushs'/'mixs'/'drys')
constraints_checked.b_content_word_closure: every content word a NEW item introduces is taught by that item, and every probe ask built by arm A's own probes_for()/probes_for_pair over new items uses only taught words, taught stems, question words or function words. The stem is taught explicitly, not derived: organs.stemming does not reduce 'cuts' to 'cut' (measured), so the frame's declared stem is the trace.
constraints_checked.c_probe_matrix_and_distractors: distractor rows scale at 0.3 per item and each is proved unanswerable: a role_swap '<q> <verb>s the <X>' is rejected if any taught item has that verb with X as its OBJECT
constraints_checked.d_registered_before_run: this block is written before any tier 120/300 artifact exists

authored.construction_rule: Keep the registered tier-40 items verbatim and in their original sessions (moving an item across a session boundary changes the interference curve, which is one of the two figures MP-E8 exists to produce). Add new items to reach the tier: tells and QA pairs in the registered 3:2 ratio, per session tier/3 split the same way. New items are drawn by random.Random(20261103).shuffle over every (subject, verb, object) combination of the registered lexicon (NAMES 15, NOUNS 67, VERBS 79 in tools/mp_e8_curriculum.py) with subject != object, taken in shuffled order, skipping any (subject, verb) pair already used by the tier. Frame: svo('<subj> <verb>s the <obj>', 'what'|'who', subj, verb, stem, obj) -- arm A's own builder, so probes_for() and the shape arbiter apply unchanged. QA pairs use the two registered ask classes 'what <verb>s the <obj>?' / 'who <verb>s the <obj>?'. Distractors at 0.3 per item (12 -> 36 -> 90), split role_swap / qword as tier 40 splits them, each one proved unanswerable against THIS tier's taught set before emit.

deviation_from_projection.reason: the projection said 136 x tier/40. Constraint (a) allows only svo frames, which yield 4 shapes per tell, while 3 of the registered 24 tells are obl/intransitive and yield 3 and 2. The registered irregulars are kept and their shapes cannot be reproduced under (a), so the matrix is proportional per item CLASS, not per total. Tier 40 re-measured through the same function returns exactly 136, which is the evidence the instrument is right and the deviation is the grammar's.

examples: 'what rings in the tower' -- 'tower' is in no taught sentence
'how many dogs sleep' -- 'many' is in no taught sentence
'when does the bell toll' -- the ask uses the stem 'toll', the answer teaches 'tolls', and a QA pair declares no stem to trace
inherited_constraint_debt.handling: reported, not repaired. Constraint (b) binds the extension, not the baseline it extends; deleting a registered probe would change the 136-row matrix arm A is sealed against, and fixing it by teaching 'tower' would change tier 40's item set. Recorded here so a reader of tier 120/300 knows the baseline is not perfect.

authored.stop_condition_status: NOT fired. The vocabulary extends without inventing words no arm could be taught: every new item teaches its own content words, and the only untaught words introduced are the registered NEVER_TAUGHT distractor nouns (harbor, orchard, cellar, attic, meadow, chapel, granary, foothill), which exist precisely to be unanswerable and scale the tier-40 'harbor was never taught' device.

tiers.battery_is_separate: The frozen battery's ask count comes from tools/scripts_heldout.json and tools/scripts_selection.json (42 asks), NOT from the bench curriculum. Tiers scale the bench; they do not automatically scale the battery, and the agent brief requires the battery once per arm as the regression guard.
tiers.named_cost: The plan asks for tiers of 40, 120 and 300 taught items with the probe matrix scaling proportionally. Only tier 40 exists, and it exists as LITERAL LISTS in tools/electric_learn_bench.py -- 24 tell-frames and 16 QA pairs typed into source. Scaling to 120 and 300 is authoring work (80 and 260 more items, each needing a taught form, probes in words the teacher never used, guarded-absence and distractor rows) plus a runtime that exceeds the 600 s shell cap by 2-10x and must be chunked. It is not a flag. See D-MPE8-03.
